preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.
The number of edges m is between n-1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(-1 <= d <= 1 for d in d)
preconditions.description: Each vertex has a degree value di that is -1, 0, or 1.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two vertices within the range 1 to n.
The number of degree values matches the number of vertices.
The number of edges matches the specified m.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or (isinstance(return_value, list) and all(isinstance(x, int) for x in return_value))
postconditions.description: The output is either '-1' or a list of integers.

postconditions.expression: return_value != '-1' or all(d[i] == -1 or d[i] == 0 for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: If no solution exists, all vertices must have degree -1 or 0.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or (len(return_value) == return_value[0] and all(1 <= x <= m for x in return_value[1:]))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the first element is the number of edges, followed by their indices within the range 1 to m.

postconditions.expression: return_value == '-1' or all((d[i] == -1 and sum(1 for u, v in edges if i+1 in (u, v) and edges.index((u, v)) + 1 in return_value[1:]) % 2 == 1) or (d[i] == 0 and sum(1 for u, v in edges if i+1 in (u, v) and edges.index((u, v)) + 1 in return_value[1:]) % 2 == 0) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, for each vertex, its degree modulo 2 matches its di value based on the selected edges.
